title: What is the Webflow Cloud?
summary: Webflow Cloud is not just a faster hosting or a minor infrastructure update. It is a complete reimagining of what you can build in Webflow.
body_text: TL;DR: Webflow Cloud is a serverless hosting platform that lets you deploy full-stack web applications (built with Next.js or Astro) directly alongside your Webflow site. It eliminates the need for separate hosting, enables programmatic SEO at scale, and brings developers, designers, and marketers together on one unified platform. Sites run on Cloudflare's global edge network with automatic scaling, 99.99% uptime, and built-in storage options. All images sourced from Memberstack’s YouTube video on the Webflow Cloud by Julian Galluzzo. What is the Webflow Cloud: Overview If you have ever built a website in Webflow, you probably loved the visual design tools. The drag-and-drop interface, the polished animations, and the ability to create beautiful sites without writing code. But if you tried pushing the platform beyond basic marketing sites, you likely encountered limitations. Webflow Cloud changes all of that. Launched in May 2025, Webflow Cloud represents a platform evolution. It is not just a faster hosting or a minor infrastructure update. It is a complete reimagining of what you can build in Webflow. Webflow Cloud enables developers to deploy web applications using frameworks like Next.js and Astro directly within their Webflow sites. This means your marketing site, your web application, your custom tools, and your dynamic content can all live under one domain, managed through one platform, without fragmented customer experiences or disconnected workflows. Key Features of Webflow Cloud Full-Stack Application Hosting Webflow Cloud supports Next.js and Astro frameworks. Deploy server-side rendered applications and complete web experiences that integrate with your Webflow-designed pages. The platform connects to GitHub for automated deployments when you push code changes. Global Edge Hosting and Unlimited Scaling Webflow Cloud uses Cloudflare's network to deliver content from data centers worldwide. Visitors get faster load times regardless of location. Bandwidth caps are removed. Sites scale automatically from 1,000 to 1 million visitors without capacity planning. This helps during traffic spikes from product launches or viral content. Dynamic Rendering with Cloudflare Workers Cloudflare Workers serve dynamic content from the edge. Build features that change based on location, time, user authentication, or other variables without performance penalties. This allows you to personalize landing pages, location-specific content, A/B testing, and real-time data displays. DevLink Integration DevLink exports Webflow components into React code. Buttons, navigation menus, forms, and layouts created in Webflow become reusable React components. Designers work in the visual environment, developers import designs as code. Cloud Storage Options Webflow Cloud provides three types of serverless storage, all deployed automatically with your application, SQLite, Key-Value Store, and Object Storage. You can mix and match these storage types based on your specific data requirements. All three are scoped to your Webflow Cloud with no vendor lock-in required. Framework Support and Future Roadmap Currently, Webflow Cloud supports Next.js and Astro within JavaScript and React. However, the goal is to be able to work over a variety of platforms in time. This means broader support for additional frameworks and libraries is planned, allowing developers to use the tools that best fit their workflows without sacrificing performance or visual control. Why It Matters: SEO, Speed, and Growth SEO & Speed Performance Google's ranking algorithm heavily weighs page speed and Core Web Vitals. Webflow Cloud's edge hosting architecture significantly improves these metrics by reducing server response times and delivering content from geographically distributed locations. Faster load times translate directly to better search rankings. Lower bounce rates result from improved user experience. Higher engagement metrics signal quality to search engines. All of these factors compound to boost your organic search visibility. Beyond speed, Webflow Cloud enables SEO at scale. You can generate thousands of landing pages dynamically from structured data without manual page creation. Think location-based pages for every city you serve, product detail pages for extensive catalogs, or long-tail keyword landing pages that would be impractical to build individually. Growth and Scalability Automatic scaling grows with your business. Launch marketing campaigns or run promotions without infrastructure concerns. Build more sophisticated experiences as you evolve: marketing sites, customer portals, internal tools, or headless ecommerce on the same platform. Real-World Use Cases Uses For Full-Stack Applications: Build advanced functionality without leaving Webflow: Booking engines : Custom reservation systems with availability checking, authentication, and payment processing Pricing calculators : Interactive tools pulling real-time API data with personalized quotes Headless ecommerce : Custom shopping experiences integrated with existing platforms SaaS onboarding : Multi-step signup flows with personalized dashboards AI integrations : Chatbots, content generation tools, and personalized recommendations Uses For Programmatic SEO: Generate thousands of pages automatically from structured data. Connect your product catalog, location database, or keyword research to deploy server-rendered, indexable pages: Location pages : Automatic generation for every city, region, or service area Long-tail campaigns : Thousands of pages targeting specific keyword variations Dynamic PPC pages : Personalized landing pages adapting to ad parameters ABM pages : Customized content for target accounts All pages live on your main domain, maintaining unified brand experience and domain authority. Uses For Internal Tools: Build custom internal systems that integrate with your site infrastructure: Employee directories : Searchable staff databases with profiles and hierarchies Content dashboards : Custom interfaces for moderation and approval workflows Analytics portals : Reporting tools with tailored visualizations Lead management : CRM-style interfaces for prospect tracking and sales coordination Real Company Example: TurboHome TurboHome, a real estate technology company, uses Webflow Cloud to deliver a personalized home-buying experience. They integrate over 200,000 MLS (Multiple Listing Service) listings through a Next.js application hosted seamlessly with their Webflow marketing site. As Rob Baldwin, CTO of TurboHome, explains in the May 2025 press release on Webflow Cloud: "Our engineering and marketing teams now work from the same system, saving time, eliminating complexity, and ensuring brand consistency across every touchpoint." This best illustrates the core value of Webflow Cloud: bringing together technical and non-technical teams on a unified platform that serves both application requirements and beautiful, on-brand marketing experiences. Security and Compliance Webflow Cloud provides enterprise-grade security: SOC 2 Type II Certification : Independent security verification GDPR-Ready Infrastructure : European privacy regulation compliance tools Audit Logs and APIs : Comprehensive tracking for compliance reporting 99.99% Uptime SLA : Reliable infrastructure SSL/TLS Encryption : Automatic HTTPS with modern encryption DDoS Protection : Built-in protection through Cloudflare This security foundation means your sites can pass legal and IT security reviews without extensive additional configuration or third-party security tools. It positions Webflow Cloud as an advanced solution without top-tier pricing for most use cases. How to Get Started and Migration Possibilities Starting Fresh with Webflow Cloud Setup takes approximately 30 minutes: Install the Webflow CLI using npm Create a new Webflow site by cloning a starter template Initialize your app using the CLI to create a Next.js or Astro application Connect to GitHub for version control and automated deployments Create a Webflow Cloud project by linking your GitHub repository Deploy by pushing your code The Webflow CLI handles much of the complexity, generating project scaffolding and connecting your development environment to Webflow's infrastructure. Migrating Existing Sites If you have an existing Webflow site, migration is straightforward. Your current site continues functioning while you add new application features. Webflow even provides a Migration Playbook for developers, agencies, and teams moving larger projects, covering edge cases, performance optimization, and best practices. Development Workflow Once set up, the workflow becomes streamlined. Designers work in Webflow's visual editor creating components and layouts. Developers import those components and build in their code editor. Content teams manage pages through Webflow's CMS interface. Deployment happens automatically when code is pushed to GitHub. Everyone works within their area of expertise using familiar tools while the platform handles integration. Webflow Cloud Cost Official Release and Pricing Webflow Cloud was officially released out of beta in July 2025 and is now available to all users. The platform implements a transparent usage-based pricing model. All paid Webflow site plans include Webflow Cloud access, with usage limits varying by plan tier. The pricing model is based on three metrics: Bandwidth : Total data transferred between your application and visitors, pooled with overall site bandwidth. Requests : Number of application requests handled monthly, including page loads, server-side executions, and API calls. CPU Time : Total compute time used to process logic and run server-side code, measured in milliseconds. Surge Pricing Protection All paid site plans include complimentary surge protection to prevent unexpected overages from traffic spikes. If you exceed your monthly allocation once, you receive notifications but face no charges. If you exceed limits again in the following month, your plan automatically upgrades at the start of your next billing cycle based on the lower usage from those two months. Plan Considerations Starter and Basic site plans have limitations: you can only mount to webflow.io domains (not custom domains), and a Webflow badge remains on your site. Higher-tier plans (CMS, Business, Enterprise) remove these restrictions and offer higher usage limits. For most professional applications, you will want at least a CMS or Business site plan. Webflow Cloud Support Documentation and Learning Resources Webflow provides extensive resources for learning and troubleshooting Webflow Cloud: Developer Documentation : Technical guides covering setup, configuration, and best practices Webflow University : Video tutorials and courses Getting Started Guides : Step-by-step walkthroughs Migration Playbooks : Documentation for moving existing sites Customer Support and Community Webflow also offers customer support via email with a 48-hour response time target. Enterprise customers receive enhanced support with faster response times and dedicated account management. The Webflow community also provides valuable assistance through an active Community Forum where users help other users solve problems, a searchable Help Center knowledge base, and a network of over 1,500 Certified Webflow Partners offering professional services and technical expertise. Conclusion Webflow Cloud bridges the gap between visual design tools and full-stack development capabilities, creating a place where designers, developers, and marketers collaborate effectively without fragmented tools or disconnected workflows. Whether you are a freelancer landing bigger projects, an agency migrating client sites, a startup needing modern infrastructure without a DevOps team, or an enterprise requiring scalable secure hosting with visual editing capabilities, Webflow Cloud offers a compelling solution. To learn more about Webflow Cloud, visit webflow.com/cloud . Frequently Asked Questions What is the difference between Webflow hosting and Webflow Cloud? Traditional Webflow hosting serves static sites and CMS-driven content with excellent performance for marketing websites and blogs. Webflow Cloud extends these capabilities by enabling full-stack applications with server-side logic, real-time data processing, complex integrations, and dynamic content generation that goes beyond static hosting limitations. Which frameworks does Webflow Cloud support? Currently, Webflow Cloud supports the JavaScript and React ecosystem, specifically Next.js and Astro frameworks. The platform's roadmap includes expanding with broader support for additional frameworks and libraries planned for future releases. Can I use Webflow Cloud with my existing Webflow site? Yes. You can add Webflow Cloud capabilities to existing Webflow sites. Your current pages continue functioning normally while you add features. Do I need coding knowledge to use Webflow Cloud? Non-technical team members do not need coding knowledge to work on the visual site components, though there are instances in which some prior knowledge may help. How does DevLink work? DevLink exports Webflow components as React code that you can import into your Webflow Cloud applications. This ensures visual elements maintain consistency and creates a unified design. What happens if I exceed my usage limits? All paid plans include surge protection. Your first overage in a billing month generates notifications but no charges, giving you time to assess usage. If you exceed limits in a second consecutive month, your plan automatically upgrades at the start of your next billing cycle based on your lower usage from those two months. Is Webflow Cloud suitable for enterprise applications? Yes. Webflow Cloud includes SOC 2 Type II certification, GDPR-ready infrastructure, audit logs, 99.99% uptime SLA, and other security features. These capabilities make it suitable for businesses with compliance requirements and high reliability needs. How do I get access to Webflow Cloud? Webflow Cloud is currently available on all paid Webflow site plans.

title: RFI Volume Is a Symptom: How Scope Gaps at Bid Drive Field RFIs
summary: Most field RFIs trace back to scope gaps at bid. Learn how pre-construction teams prevent RFI volume by closing gaps before award.
body_text: TL;DR Most field RFIs don't start in the field. They start during bid when scope is left vague or undefined. According to FMI, $31 billion in annual U.S. rework comes from miscommunication and bad project data — scope gaps are the primary driver. The Arcadis 2025 Global Construction Disputes Report puts the average U.S. construction dispute value at $60.1M. "Errors and omissions in contract documents" has been the #1 dispute cause for 6 of the last 9 years. Pre-construction teams that close scope gaps before award — not after — reduce RFI volume, change order exposure, and field conflict. Five habits separate low-RFI projects from high-RFI ones. They all live in pre-con. The RFI Problem Starts Earlier Than You Think When RFI volume spikes on a project, the instinct is to look at the field. Maybe the super isn't coordinating well. Maybe the subs are fishing for change orders. Maybe the design team is slow to respond. Those things happen. But they're rarely the root cause. Most high-RFI projects trace back to a single failure point: scope that wasn't defined clearly enough at bid. The field is just where the gap surfaces. The gap itself was created weeks or months earlier — in the estimate room, in the scope package, in the subcontract. This article breaks down how that happens and what pre-construction teams can do to stop it. What a Scope Gap Actually Is A scope gap is any work required to complete the project that isn't clearly assigned to a responsible party. It's not always missing work. Sometimes it's work that two subs both think the other is doing. Sometimes it's work that the spec references but no scope package captures. Sometimes it's work that's "readily inferable" — and your subcontract language just handed it to you. Scope gaps come in three forms: Coverage gaps: Work that nobody's scope includes. A trade falls through the cracks entirely. Overlap gaps: Two subs both exclude the same item, each assuming it's the other's responsibility. The RFI reveals the standoff. Vagueness gaps: The scope says "as per plans and specs." Nobody checked whether the plans and specs actually agree with each other. All three end up as field RFIs. And all three were preventable at bid. How Scope Gaps Become Field RFIs Here's the chain reaction most pre-con teams know but rarely map out explicitly: Bid-day pressure compresses review time. Scope packages are written from templates, not drawings. Review happens five minutes before cutoff, if at all. Vague scopes get priced vaguely. Subs exclude anything ambiguous to protect margin. Nobody surfaces the ambiguity at bid. The subcontract is written to match the scope package. If the scope package has gaps, the subcontract does too. The gap hits the field. Work needs to happen. Nobody's scope covers it. An RFI gets issued — sometimes to clarify responsibility, sometimes to set up a change order claim. The dispute starts. The GC looks at the subcontract. The sub points to the scope. Nobody has a clear answer because the answer was never written down. A Pre-Construction Lead at a Top-ENR Canadian GC put it plainly: "If you miss anything, they'll bill it." That billing starts with an RFI. Real Examples: What Scope Gaps Actually Cost These aren't hypotheticals. They're anonymized examples drawn from over 200 GC interviews conducted for The Scope Gap Playbook . $300K in Lead-Lined Glass A hospital imaging suite required lead-lined glass. The spec called for it. The drawings showed it. Nobody's scope package explicitly assigned it. The GC absorbed the cost under "readily inferable" language in the subcontract. One RFI, one scope gap, $300K out of pocket. $400K Roof Cover Board On a $50M project, roof cover board wasn't captured in the envelope scope package. The gap was discovered in the field. The GC recovered the cost only through a relational concession from the sub — not because the subcontract gave them any leverage. $45K Stone-Depth Mismatch Civil, structural, and architectural drawings disagreed on slab stone depth. Nobody reconciled them at bid. The discrepancy surfaced as a field RFI. The resolution cost $45K and two weeks of coordination time. Each of these started as a scope gap at bid. Each ended as a field problem — an RFI, a change order, or a dispute. For more trade-specific examples like these, see the trade-specific scope gaps chapter of The Scope Gap Playbook. Why "As Per Plans and Specs" Is the Most Expensive Phrase in Construction It's the most common anti-pattern in scope writing. The scope package says "as per plans and specs." The sub prices it that way. Nobody checks whether the plans and specs actually align — or whether they contradict each other. This phrase doesn't define scope. It defers it. And deferred scope becomes an RFI the moment the field needs an answer. A Director of Pre-Construction at a Mid-Market Southeast GC described the disconnect this way: "Pre-con is working in the scope sheet world and project management is working in the scopes of work." The gap between those two worlds is where RFIs live. The Pre-Construction Lead at a Top-ENR Canadian GC calls it the "peanut-butter test": "It's descriptive — bread, put it on a plate, use the open jar… You have to get to that level of detail or else they'll just be like, 'you didn't tell us that.'" Most scope packages don't pass that test. The Anti-Patterns That Create RFI Volume Based on the same 200+ GC interviews, The Scope Gap Playbook identifies the habits that consistently produce high-RFI projects. These aren't edge cases — they show up across firm size, geography, and project type. "As per plans and specs" — assigns nothing, assumes everything. Copy-paste from the previous similar job — last job's scope doesn't match this job's drawings. Junior estimators stuffing previous scopes verbatim — no drawing review, no reconciliation. The five-minutes-before-bid review — no time to catch gaps, let alone close them. Generic inferred-scope laundry lists — broad language that sounds thorough but assigns nothing specifically. Trusting subs on a gentleman's agreement — works until it doesn't. An Estimating Manager at a Canadian ICI GC noted: "We have less subs who just kind of a gentleman's agreement… they've become more quick to clarify that we're not including that one piece of scope." Each of these habits produces ambiguity. Ambiguity produces RFIs. Five Habits That Reduce RFI Volume — Before the Project Starts The firms with the lowest RFI volume on delivery don't manage RFIs better in the field. They prevent them in pre-con. Here's what they do differently. 1. Start With Drawings, Not Boilerplate Scope packages built from templates carry the previous project's assumptions. Scope packages built from the actual drawing set reflect what this project actually requires. The difference shows up in field RFI counts. Review the drawings first. Build the scope to match. Then apply the template as a floor — not a starting point. 2. Use Specific Document References Don't write "as per plans and specs." Write "per Structural Drawing S-301, Rev 2, and Spec Section 03300." Specific references leave no room for interpretation disputes. They also make RFI responses faster when questions do arise. 3. Front-Load the Buyout Conversations Scope gaps between bid and buyout are a major RFI driver. When what the sub priced doesn't match what the GC's scope package says, the field pays for it. Front-loading buyout conversations — before award, not after — closes those gaps while there's still budget flexibility to address them. 4. Tailor Scopes to Sub Sophistication A national mechanical contractor reads scope differently than a regional HVAC shop. The level of detail required in the scope package should match the sub's sophistication — and their history of RFI and change order behavior on past projects. Generic scope packages ignore this entirely. 5. Run a Pre-Issue Scope Review Before the scope package goes out, someone who didn't write it should read it against the drawings. Not for grammar. For gaps. This is the checkpoint most teams skip — and it's the cheapest place to catch a $300K problem. These five habits map directly to the Eight Habits framework in The Scope Gap Playbook , which covers the full set of practices that separate low-gap from high-gap pre-construction teams. Trade-Specific Gaps That Drive the Most RFIs Not all trades produce equal RFI volume. Some scope areas are structurally more prone to gaps — because the work crosses trade boundaries, because the spec language is ambiguous, or because the drawings from different disciplines conflict. Trade Common Gap Typical RFI Trigger MEP Generator field conditioning, motor starters, fire-rated louvres Who owns the work? GC or sub? Concrete Base plate grouting, slab assembly conflicts, concrete pumping Spec and drawing don't agree on method Steel Embeds and anchor bolts, hoisting and rigging, misc metals Scope boundary between structural steel and other trades Envelope Roof cover board, masonry-storefront flashings, fire-stopping Nobody's scope explicitly assigns the interface work Drywall Wall blocking, gypcrete naming collision, hollow metal frames Two subs, one item, no clear owner Site/Earthwork Geotech compaction, the five-foot transition, unit-rate exploitation Ambiguity in geotech report vs. scope language MEP is particularly high-risk. Generator field conditioning costs alone have generated "millions" in disputed claims, recurring across multiple projects at the same firms. The pattern is consistent: the scope doesn't assign it, both parties assume the other owns it, and the field RFI turns into a change order battle. See the full breakdown in the trade-specific scope gaps chapter . What Pre-Construction Teams Are Doing About It in 2026 The firms taking RFI reduction seriously in 2026 are attacking it at the source — in pre-con, not in the field. A few specific shifts are happening: Drawing-based scope generation: Teams are moving away from template-first scope writing. They're reviewing drawings before building scope packages — or using tools that do the drawing review for them. Cross-discipline conflict checks: Structural, civil, and architectural drawings often disagree. Catching those conflicts at bid is cheaper than resolving them as field RFIs. Explicit scope language for gray areas: The gentleman's agreement is gone. Subs are tighter on exclusions. GCs are responding with more explicit scope language — or paying for the ambiguity later. Tools like Scope Agent are part of this shift. Scope Agent reads the full project set — drawings, specs, and addenda — and generates a complete scope-of-work package in under 60 minutes. It surfaces cross-discipline conflicts, flags missing trade coverage, and produces structured outputs that estimators can review and refine. That's work that used to take 30–40 hours manually — and often didn't happen at all on smaller pursuits. Teams using Provision have reviewed over $100 billion in project value and processed more than 66,000 documents. The scope gaps that surface aren't edge cases — they're consistent, trade-specific patterns that repeat project to project. If your team is managing RFI volume reactively — tracking them in a log, managing response time, escalating to the design team — you're working the symptom. The fix is earlier. It's in the scope package, at bid, before award. A Senior PM at a Toronto Mid-Market Developer put it this way: "If we could catch three scope gaps or three missed items on every scope of work, then this thing pays for itself." That math works. Every scope gap you close at bid is an RFI you never have to write, a change order you never have to fight, and margin you don't have to give back. To see how Scope Agent works on a real project set, book a demo with the Provision team. Frequently Asked Questions What is the root cause of high RFI volume on construction projects? Most high-RFI projects trace back to scope gaps created during bid. When scope packages are vague, built from templates rather than drawings, or use language like "as per plans and specs," ambiguity gets baked in. That ambiguity surfaces in the field as RFIs — often weeks or months after the gap was created. How does a scope gap become a field RFI? A scope gap leaves work unassigned or ambiguously assigned. When that work needs to happen in the field, the team issues an RFI to get a direction or establish responsibility. If the subcontract mirrors the vague scope package, that RFI often turns into a change order dispute. Which trades produce the most RFIs from scope gaps? MEP, concrete, steel, and envelope work consistently generate the most scope-gap-driven RFIs. Interface work — where two trades share a boundary — is especially high-risk. Generator field conditioning, base plate grouting, roof cover board, and masonry-storefront flashings are common examples where scope falls through the cracks. What does "readily inferable" language mean for GCs? Many subcontracts include language requiring subs to perform work that is "readily inferable" from the contract documents — even if it isn't explicitly called out in the scope package. In practice, this means the GC absorbs cost for anything the documents imply but the scope doesn't assign. The $300K lead-lined glass example is a real case of this playing out on a hospital project. How can pre-construction teams reduce RFI volume before a project starts? Five habits have the biggest impact: starting scope packages from drawings rather than templates, using specific document references instead of "as per plans and specs," front-loading buyout conversations, tailoring scope detail to sub sophistication, and running a pre-issue scope review before the package goes out.
